name: 9 changed client modules staged with no mapped test — QA gate stops at require_approval
description:
Finding (QA, shift 2026-11-18, card 88d57bdd owns the staged tree):

`qa_review_changes(scope="staged")` on the 21-file / +2135 staged diff returns **require_approval** (highest_severity medium, 10 findings). Nine changed client sources are unmapped and none is declared in `qa_policy.ignore_paths`:

- client/src/components/browsers/CoworkingFileBrowser.vue
- client/src/components/browsers/CoworkingFoldersBrowser.vue
- client/src/components/browsers/CoworkingVolumeExplorer.vue
- client/src/components/browsers/CoworkingVolumeMappings.vue
- client/src/components/browsers/volumeMappings.js
- client/src/components/chat/ChatFindBar.vue
- client/src/utils/chatFind.js
- client/src/utils/taskActivity.js
- client/src/views/GlobalSettings.vue

The 10th finding is `tests.run-error` and is NOT test-writing work: the gate passes repo-root-relative paths to suite `pytest:api` (cwd `api/`) and pytest exits 5 (nothing collected). Tracked on card e5841226 — do not try to fix it here.

What to do:
1. Add or extend unit tests naming each of the 9 modules (the gate matches by module name in the test file, e.g. a test file that mentions `chatFind`). Pure helper modules first (`chatFind.js`, `taskActivity.js`, `volumeMappings.js`) — highest value, cheapest to cover.
2. For any module that genuinely carries no behaviour worth a unit test, propose an explicit `qa_policy.ignore_paths` entry with a written reason for the user to approve. Never skip/xfail a test to make the gate pass.

Acceptance criteria:
- `qa_review_changes(scope="staged", suite="pytest:api")` → `mapped_sources` >= 10 (currently 1) and no `change.missing-tests` findings for the 9 paths above.
- The new tests must pass standalone: `qa_run_tests(suite="pytest", paths=["<new test files>"])` → failed 0.

Do not edit product code; if a module's behaviour contradicts its test, raise it to software_developer instead.

1. Add or extend unit tests naming each of the 9 modules (the gate matches by module name in the test file, e.g. a test file that mentions `chatFind`). Pure helper modules first (`chatFind.js`, `taskActivity.js`, `volumeMappings.js`) — highest value, cheapest to cover.

Acceptance criteria:

Do not edit product code; if a module's behaviour contradicts its test, raise it to software_developer instead.

Root cause of this card's finding, from the environment side (QA, shift 2026-11-18):

The 9 client modules are not merely "untested" — they are **untestable in this runtime**:
- `qa_plan` declares only `pytest`, `pytest:api`, `npm:wiki`. There is **no client suite** for `client/`.
- `npm:wiki` reports `available=False`, reason `npm not found in PATH` → the only JS suite is unrunnable too.

So this card cannot be closed by writing tests alone; the environment must first gain a runnable client suite (tracked as a separate HIGH env card created this shift: "No runnable test suite for client/ — 9 staged client modules are unverifiable").

Gate behaviour to keep in mind: `qa_review_changes(scope="staged")` = `require_approval`, mapping **1/10**, `change.missing-tests` x9. It will keep returning that until either the suite exists or the paths are declared in `qa_policy.ignore_paths` with a rationale.

## Sequencing ruling from ProjectManager (shift 3, 2026-11-18) — read before you start

**This card is blocked until `e09bcf77` lands.** Do not spend your run writing tests before that card is closed.

Why: `e09bcf77` (HIGH, same parent shift as this card) establishes that the runtime has **no runnable client suite and `npm` is not in PATH** (`qa_plan` → `npm:wiki available=False`). Writing the 9 test files first means they can never be **executed** — and this card's own acceptance criterion is `qa_run_tests(...) → failed 0`. You cannot satisfy acceptance criteria in an environment with no runner. Writing unexecutable tests to turn a gate green is the same failure mode as skipping them.

**Order of work:**
1. `e09bcf77` — provision `npm` and declare a client suite (e.g. vitest, `cwd=client`) so `qa_plan` reports `available=True`.
2. **Then** this card — pure helpers first (`chatFind.js`, `taskActivity.js`, `volumeMappings.js`): cheapest, highest value, no component mounting needed.
3. Then the 6 `.vue` components (`CoworkingFileBrowser`, `CoworkingFoldersBrowser`, `CoworkingVolumeExplorer`, `CoworkingVolumeMappings`, `ChatFindBar`, `GlobalSettings`).
4. Anything genuinely not worth a unit test → propose a dated `qa_policy.ignore_paths` entry **with a written rationale for the user to approve**. Never `skip`/`xfail` to make the gate pass.

**Scope guard:** the 10th finding (`tests.run-error`, pytest exit 5 / nothing collected because repo-root-relative paths hit a `cwd=api` suite) is **not** yours — it is card `e5841226`. Do not "fix" it by loosening the suite.

**Environment guard:** the 9 paths are under `client/`, which is **not in this `codx-api` working tree** (`project_changes` shows no `client/**` entries here) — they live in `codx-junior-platform`. Work in that project; do not add a `client/` tree to `codx-api` to make the gate pass.

Also: **do not use `project_locate` / `project_map` / `project_trace` / `read_folder`** — they time out at 120 s on this repo (`d8534b12`).

**QA shift 5 (2026-11-18) — the staged scope measured again, and it is the same 9 modules**

`qa_review_changes(scope="staged", run_tests=false)` this shift:

- decision `require_approval`, `highest_severity: medium`, **9 findings**
- `changed_files: 28`, `test_files: 144`, **`mapped_sources: 1`**, **`unmapped_sources: 9`**
- the 9 unmapped are, verbatim, the staged `client/` modules:
  `client/src/components/browsers/CoworkingFileBrowser.vue`,
  `CoworkingFoldersBrowser.vue`, `CoworkingVolumeExplorer.vue`,
  `CoworkingVolumeMappings.vue`, `volumeMappings.js`,
  `client/src/components/chat/ChatFindBar.vue`,
  `client/src/utils/chatFind.js`,
  `client/src/utils/taskActivity.js`,
  `client/src/views/GlobalSettings.vue`

Conclusion unchanged and now measured on the *staged* subset as well as the working tree (`scope="all"`: 220 files, 35 mapped / 58 unmapped / 11 findings):

- **No test can be added for these 9 today** — `qa_plan` lists exactly three suites (`pytest`, `pytest:api` at cwd `api/`, `npm:wiki`) and `npm:wiki` is `available: false` ("npm not found in PATH"). There is no `client` suite, so the gate cannot be satisfied by writing tests; it can only be satisfied by declaring these paths in `qa_policy.ignore_paths` **with a reason**.
- That is a **policy decision, not a QA action**: the mandate says a blocked verdict is fixed by code or by a dated user approval of the policy change. The ignore_paths entry for `client/src/**` needs the user's dated approval and the reason written next to it (e.g. "client has no test runner in this runtime; tracked by e09bcf77").
- Note the newly found read-side gap (new card this shift): `qa_policy(action="show")` prints only `enabled / min_coverage / block_above / fail_closed`, so **`ignore_paths` cannot be read back** — whoever applies the declaration cannot verify it from the tool; they can only watch the finding disappear.

Re-verification: `qa_review_changes(scope="staged", run_tests=false)` → expect **0** `change.missing-tests` findings once the 9 paths are declared (or a `client` jest/vitest suite exists, which needs `e09bcf77` first).
